title: Osteo-REAL
summary:
As people age, bone strength decreases. This can initially lead to osteopenia (a precursor stage) and, as it progresses, to osteoporosis, in which fractures can occur even with minor stress. After such a fracture, there is an increased risk of further fractures, particularly within the first year afterwards. Besides the individual suffering of those affected, this also creates a considerable burden on the healthcare system, including health and long-term care insurers, as well as an increasing burden on treating institutions. Although effective medications and clear treatment recommendations are available, Germany still lacks, compared to other European countries, nationwide, well-organised follow-up care after a fracture.
In Munich, there is a particularly good care situation compared to the rest of Germany: university institutions of the LMU University Hospital and community-based physicians already work closely together, so that care between hospital and practice functions comparatively well, even though there is still potential for improvement. This favourable starting situation will be used within the study to first capture the actual, everyday care of patients. Building on this, the study aims to identify opportunities to improve care and to develop modern, digital solutions to make treatment more efficient and better connected in the future.

OSTEO-REAL is a multicentre, intersectoral, and ambispective observational study designed to capture the real-world care of patients with osteopenia and osteoporosis. The study is conducted at two sites: the specialised osteology centre of the LMU University Hospital and a cooperating specialised osteological practice in the community-based outpatient setting. At enrolment, both study-relevant retrospective data from the patient's clinical history and continuously collected prospective data are recorded using REDCap. The required data are obtained from the medical records of the LMU University Hospital, the participating specialised osteological practice, established patient questionnaires, and external reports from physicians, hospitals, therapists, and rehabilitation and nursing care facilities. Data collection corresponds to routine clinical care; there are no study-specific interventions.
At both sites, two patient groups are considered, so that the study comprises four groups in total.
In all four groups, the same information is collected, which would in any case be gathered as part of standard treatment: information on the disease, on treatment, on medications and their regular use, on falls, on mobility, and on quality of life.

Adults aged 18 years and older who are able to make their own decision regarding participation can take part. Persons who are unable to make this decision themselves, who require a high level of nursing care, or in whom a rare, genetically determined bone disease has already been diagnosed cannot participate.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age ≥18 years
Capacity to consent
Exclusion criteria:
Minors and lack of capacity to consent
Dementia
Legal guardianship
Severe comorbidities that make participation impossible (e.g., hospitalisation, nursing home residency, bedriddenness). These patients are considered separately within the scope of an already approved study (Project No.: 25-0120, Dr. Vera Smolka).
Substance abuse
Rare skeletal disorders (Note: Only patients with a previously confirmed monogenic disease are excluded. Patients in whom no genetic disease was initially known but who are diagnosed with one during the course of the study are included in the OSTEO-REAL study and separately documented.)
